core_obligations: (1)(a) implies (1)(b) (proof lines 7710-7724): with the colimit X and the maps X -> M_i taken from the definition, the full subcategory on the targets of morphisms with source i is cofinal and filtered; for i' in it the composite X -> M_i -> M_{i'} -> X is the identity on X, so Karoubian-ness gives M_{i'} = X_{i'} + Z_{i'} with Z_{i'} the kernel of M_{i'} -> X; choosing k receiving both i and i' as in the definition shows that M_{i'} -> M_k annihilates Z_{i'}.

(1)(b) implies (1)(a) (proof lines 7726-7743): one may first replace the index category by the cofinal I'; defining X -> M_i as the inverse of the isomorphism X_{i'} -> X followed by the inclusion, the author shows that for any two objects i and j and suitable morphisms to k and then l the composites M_j -> X -> M_i -> M_l and M_j -> M_l agree, which is exactly essential constancy.
(2) (proof lines 7745-7746): the cofiltered statement is the dual of the filtered one, whose two directions are both written out in full inside the counted span.
proof_roadmap: Get the direct summand decomposition from Karoubian-ness of the target category, using the composite through the colimit.
Use cofinality and the second condition in the definition of essential constancy to kill the complementary summand.
Reverse the implication by replacing the index category with the cofinal subcategory and computing two composites.
difficulty_reason: The lemma characterizes an essentially constant diagram with values in a pre-additive Karoubian category by the existence of a colimit (or limit) and of a cofinal (or initial) subcategory on which the diagram splits as a constant part mapping isomorphically to the colimit plus a part eventually killed (statement lines 7683-7707). The proof is a complete argument for the filtered case in both directions: the splitting comes from Karoubian-ness applied to the composite through the colimit and the complementary summand is annihilated by a suitable map chosen through the definition of essential constancy (proof lines 7710-7724); the converse replaces the index category by the cofinal subcategory and compares two composites (proof lines 7726-7743). The non-formal content is the production of the splitting and the two-object comparison. The claim is H2: a structured argument with each input named.
